summary: Five Tribes is a clever mancala-style worker-placement game where players move meeples already on the board to trigger effects, collect resources, and control tiles and djinns for scoring combos. The Djinns of Naqala expansion adds new djinn cards and a resource-based scoring djinn, deepening the combo potential without changing the core flow.
praised: Tight, tense auction for turn order
Rich combo potential between tiles, resources, and djinns
Beautiful production and satisfying meeple manipulation
criticised: Can suffer from analysis paralysis, especially with more players
Auction-based turn order can feel punishing to less experienced players
Late-game moves are heavily constrained by board state
Take-that elements (assassins) can feel harsh to newer players

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial on a shared board
interaction.detail: All meeples and tiles sit on one shared board, and every move changes what's available to the next player, so positioning and denying good moves to opponents is central. Players also bid against each other for turn order and can directly attack opponents' meeples with assassins.

scoring.why: Points accrue from several separate systems: Vizier and Elder meeples collected, goods sold from Merchant meeples, palaces/palm trees built by Builders, gold held, and Djinn cards acquired, with Assassins instead used to remove rivals' meeples.
scoring.how_you_win: You bid for turn order, then move a group of meeples across the shared board (Mancala-style) to collect same-colored meeples and trigger the tile's effect, building up a hidden gold total and card/tile bonuses; the player with the highest combined score when the board is depleted wins.

_name: Five Tribes: The Djinns of Naqala
